title: Wear
subtitle: 本課集中處理 wear = clothing / footwear / accessories on the body 的義項。 最重要的區別是 state vs action：w
description: 本課集中處理 wear = clothing / footwear / accessories on the body 的義項。 最重要的區別是 state vs action：wear / have on / be wearing 描述已經穿着的狀態；put on / don 描述『穿上／戴上』的動作。另一些表達則強調整體服裝風格或顯眼展示。

words.example: She had a dark blue coat on when she arrived.
words.exampleZh: 她到達時穿着一件深藍色外套。

exercises.upgrade: She had a long coat on when I saw her.

options.explanation: Have on ✓ — be wearing a particular item of clothing, footwear, or accessory. Here, the sentence describes what was already on her body at that moment. That makes Have on the most precise replacement for this particular sense of wear.

Be wearing — have clothing, footwear, jewellery, or another item on the body at a particular time. This is good for a temporary wearing state, but it does not express the action of putting something on or an overall style of dress. The decisive clue is that the sentence describes what was already on her body at that moment.

Put on — place clothing, footwear, or an accessory on the body. This is eventive: it means starting to wear something, so it cannot replace a sentence that only describes an existing wearing state. The decisive clue is that the sentence describes what was already on her body at that moment.
Carry — have something with you or transport it. Carrying something does not mean it is worn on the body. The decisive clue is that the sentence describes what was already on her body at that moment.

Hold — keep something in the hands or in a position. Holding something is a hand/position action, not wearing. The decisive clue is that the sentence describes what was already on her body at that moment.
Use — employ something for a purpose. This is far too broad and does not specify clothing or accessories. The decisive clue is that the sentence describes what was already on her body at that moment.

Use — employ something for a purpose. This is far too broad and does not specify clothing or accessories. The decisive clue is that formal descriptive imagery is central.

exercises.original: The figures were wearing black from head to toe.
exercises.zh: 那些人從頭到腳都穿着黑色衣服。
exercises.upgrade: The figures were clad in black from head to toe.

options.explanation: Be dressed in — be wearing a particular set, colour, style, or type of clothing. This describes overall clothing and is awkward for single accessories or putting-on actions. The decisive clue is that literary full-body clothing description is intended.

Sport — wear or display a noticeable item, style, or appearance. This adds a noticeable/display nuance and is too marked for ordinary clothing. The decisive clue is that literary full-body clothing description is intended.
Carry — have something with you or transport it. Carrying something does not mean it is worn on the body. The decisive clue is that literary full-body clothing description is intended.
Hold — keep something in the hands or in a position. Holding something is a hand/position action, not wearing. The decisive clue is that literary full-body clothing description is intended.

falseSynonyms.zh: 攜帶 ≠ wear carry 表示拿着／帶着，不代表物件在身上穿戴。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Carry is about possession/transport.

falseSynonyms.zh: 使用 ≠ wear use 太廣；穿戴是使用某物的一種方式，但不是同義。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Use is much broader.

falseSynonyms.zh: 拿着 ≠ wear hold 表示手持，不是穿戴。
只在『穿上』動作 sense 接近 put on 表示開始穿戴，不是穿着狀態。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Put on is eventive.

falseSynonyms.zh: 穿衣／給……穿衣 ≠ 所有 wear dress 可指穿衣這個行為或給某人穿衣，語法不同。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Dress has different grammar.

falseSynonyms.zh: 只在顯眼展示 sense 接近 sport 有展示／顯眼語氣，不是所有 wear 都自然。
給……穿衣 ≠ wear clothe 通常是給另一個人穿衣或提供衣物。
不規則變化陷阱 wear–wore–worn；不要把 worn 當作一般現在式。
